# Proverbs 14 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** A wise woman builds her home, but a foolish one tears it apart with her own hands.

**2** If you walk with integrity, you honor the LORD. If you're crooked in how you live, you're showing contempt for Him.

**3** A fool's arrogant words invite punishment, but the wise protect themselves by how they speak.

**4** An empty barn stays clean — but you don't get a harvest without oxen.

**5** A reliable witness tells the truth. A dishonest one does nothing but lie.

**6** A cynic looks for wisdom and never finds it, but for someone with understanding, knowledge comes easily.

**7** Walk away from a fool — you won't learn anything useful from them.

**8** The wisdom of a sensible person is knowing where they're going. The 'wisdom' of fools is self-deception.

**9** Fools treat guilt like a joke, but among honest people there is genuine goodwill.

**10** Only your own heart knows how deep your pain goes, and no one else can fully share your joy either.

**11** The wicked person's impressive house will be demolished, but even the humble tent of the upright will flourish.

**12** There's a path that looks perfectly right to a person — but it ends in death.

**13** Even during laughter, the heart can be hurting. And sometimes joy ends in sorrow.

**14** People who turn away from what's right will get the full consequences. And people who do good will be rewarded in full.

**15** A naive person believes everything they hear, but a shrewd person thinks carefully about every step.

**16** A wise person is careful and avoids danger, but a fool charges ahead recklessly, full of confidence.

**17** A short-tempered person does foolish things, and a calculating schemer is despised.

**18** The gullible end up wearing foolishness like a garment, but the perceptive wear knowledge like a crown.

**19** Eventually, evil people will bow before good ones — the wicked will stand at the gates of the righteous.

**20** Nobody wants to be around poor people — even their neighbors avoid them. But everyone wants to be friends with the rich.

**21** Looking down on your neighbor is wrong. But showing kindness to those in need — that person is truly blessed.

**22** People who plot harm will go astray, but those who plan to do good will be met with love and faithfulness.

**23** All hard work leads to something, but all talk and no action leads to nothing.

**24** Wealth is what the wise have to show for their work, but fools produce nothing but more foolishness.

**25** An honest witness saves lives, but a liar is deadly.

**26** When you honor the LORD, you stand on solid ground — and your children will find safety there too.

**27** Honoring the LORD is like drinking from a spring of life — it keeps you from stepping into deadly traps.

**28** A king's greatness depends on the size of his nation. A leader without people has nothing.

**29** Being slow to get angry shows deep understanding, but a hot temper only magnifies foolishness.

**30** Inner peace gives health to the whole body, but jealousy is a disease that rots you from the inside.

**31** Exploiting the poor is an insult to their Creator. But showing kindness to those in need honors God directly.

**32** The wicked are brought down by their own wrongdoing, but the righteous have something solid to hold onto even in death.

**33** Wisdom settles quietly in the heart of the understanding, but among fools it has to make itself loud to be noticed.

**34** Righteousness lifts a whole nation, but sin drags any people down into disgrace.

**35** A competent worker earns the boss's respect, but an incompetent one gets their anger.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **14:4**: This is one of the most practical verses in the Bible — you can't have productivity without mess. An empty stable is clean but useless.

- **14:10**: Deeply true: no one fully knows what you're going through. Your deepest pain and your deepest joy are ultimately private.

- **14:12**: This is a terrifying verse — the path to death can look completely right. Self-deception doesn't feel like deception; that's what makes it deadly.

— PNEUMA
